1.q: The Spirit of God came on Azariah
1.note: This is an idiom which means that the spirit of God influenced Azariah and enabled him to prophesy. Alternate translation: [The Spirit of God gave Azariah the ability to prophesy]
This is the name of a man.

2.q: he will be found by you
2.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you will find him] or [he will permit you to find him]

3.q: Israel was without the true God
3.note: Here “Israel” refers to the people of Israel. This refers to a time when the people of Israel did not worship the true God. Alternate translation: [The people of Israel did not worship the true God]
Alternate translation: [without a priest who taught them]

4.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [they found him] or [he permitted them to find him]

5.q: for him who traveled away, nor for him who traveled to here
5.note: This phrase is an idiom that refers to a person who travels anywhere away from home. Alternate translation: [for the person who traveled anywhere]

5.q: great troubles were on all the inhabitants of the lands
5.note: The people experiencing great troubles is spoken of as if those troubles were objects that were on the people. Alternate translation: [all the inhabitants of the lands experienced great troubles]

6.q: They were broken in pieces, nation against nation, and city against city
6.note: The word “they” refers to the words “nation” and “city.” Conquering one another is spoken of as if they were breaking each other into pieces. Alternate translation: [Nations and cities destroyed each other, nations fighting nations, cities fighting cities]

6.q: They were broken in pieces, nation against nation, and city against city
6.note: Here “nation” and “city” are metonyms for the people who live there. You may also supply a connecting word to clarify the relationship between these two phrases. Alternate translation: [Nations and cities destroyed each other, as the people of one nation fought against the people of another nation, and the people of one city fought against the people of another city] (See also: [Connecting Words and Phrases](ta:grammar-connect-words-phrases))

7.q: do not let your hands be weak
7.note: Here the word “hands” represents the people who work. Alternate translation: [do not become weak as you work]

7.q: for your work will be rewarded
7.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Yahweh is the implied subject. Alternate translation: [for Yahweh will reward your work] (See also: [Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information](ta:figs-explicit))

8.q: When Asa heard these words, the prophecy of Oded the prophet
8.note: The word translated as **food** represents the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense because REASON. Scholars have proposed that a scribe may have added the wrong vowels to the original consonants of the text, resulting in this word. With different vowels, it would say “deformity,” which seems to fit better the meaning of this passage. The UST follows that interpretation. You may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [deformity]

8.q: the prophecy of Oded the prophet
8.note: Many versions, including the UST, make this passage read, “the prophecy of Azariah, the son of Oded the prophet.” They do this in order to make the sense agree with [2 Chronicles 15:1](ta:15). Translators will probably want to do the same in their versions.

The words “the disgusting things” refers to idols. Having his people remove or destroy the idols is spoken of as if it were driving them away. Alternate translation: [got rid of the disgusting idols] (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

9.q: He gathered all Judah and Benjamin
9.note: Here the word “all” is a generalization. The phrase means that David assembled people from all over Judah and Benjamin. Alternate translation: [He gathered together people from all over Judah and Benjamin]
Alternate translation: [For people from of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon came from Israel]

10.note: “They” here refers to the tribes of Judah and Israel that were with Asa.
This is the third month of the Hebrew calendar. It is during the last part of May and the first part of June on Western calendars.

11.q: some of the plunder that they had brought
11.note: This refers to the plunder that they had taken from the villages around Gerar in 2 Chronicles 14:14.

12.q: with all their heart and with all their soul
12.note: Together, these two phrases form an idiomatic expression that refers to a person’s entire being. Alternate translation: [with all their beings] or [wholeheartedly] (See also: [Doublet](ta:figs-doublet))

13.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [should die]

13.q: whether the person was small or great
13.note: This could mean: (1) a person’s importance within the community is spoken of as if the person were small or great. Alternate translation: [whether the person was important or not] or (2) a young person is spoken of as if he were small and an old person is spoken of as if he were great. Alternate translation: [whether the person was young or old]

15.note: Here the word “all” is a generalization. The phrase means that people from all over Judah rejoiced. Alternate translation: [People all over Judah rejoiced]
The idiom “with all their heart” means “with complete devotion.” Alternate translation: [with complete devotion] or [wholeheartedly]

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. See how you translated this in 2 Chronicles 15:4. Alternate translation: [they found him] or [he permitted them to find him]

16.note: This phrase refers to an idol.

16.q: Asa cut down the disgusting figure, ground it … and burned it
16.note: Since Asa was king, he may have told his officials to cut down the figure. Alternate translation: [Asa made his workers cut down the disgusting figure, grind it … and burn it]

17.q: But the high places were not taken out of Israel
17.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [But Asa did not command the people to take the high places out of Israel]
The heart represents the person. Alternate translation: [Asa was completely devoted]
This refers to the whole period of time that Asa lived. Alternate translation: [the whole time that he lived] or [throughout his whole life]

18.note: Here the word “house” represents the temple. Alternate translation: [the temple of God]
